- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean-reversion correction toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for days 6–30.
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.33 or lower), model tends to ignore trend; apply downward bias correction of 5–10% for next 7–14 days.
